discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in c739776f. Agreed on the root cause: `resolveAccountApiBaseUrl` prefers the provider `baseUrl`, while the link used `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl`, so a staging override with `CLINE_ENVIRONMENT` unset opened production.

`@cline/shared` now exports `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`, which maps the resolved backend to the environment that declares it (trailing slash ignored). The CLI resolves the account backend once, passes that exact base URL to `createClineAccountService`, and builds the link from `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`. A backend no environment declares (proxy, self-hosted) resolves to `undefined`, and `getClinePrivacySettingsUrl` now hides the link in that case instead of opening a different environment.

The same mismatch existed in the desktop sidecar `get_cline_app_base_url`, so it uses the same helper now. Tests: `resolveClineAppBaseUrl` (shared), `loadClineAccountSnapshot` links to `staging-app.cline.bot` for a staging override and hides the link for an unmatched backend, and the sidecar command returns `https://staging-app.cline.bot` / `undefined` likewise.

Fixed in 67cdb9112 for the CLI install: `ollama serve` is now started with `OLLAMA_HOST` set from the saved URL (checked by starting it on port 11599). The macOS and Windows apps read their own settings and ignore our environment, so a custom port there still has to be set in Ollama itself.

Valid catch, thanks. Fixed in 7f194e9: the Bedrock exclusion list moved from `vendors/bedrock.ts` into `@cline/llms` as `isProviderApiKeyEnv()`, which both the Bedrock runtime and this helper now use, so the TUI skips the same non-key variables the runtime skips. The environment key is also passed through `isProviderSettingsUsable()` as a stand-in for a saved key, so provider-specific requirements (Bedrock region, Vertex project, Azure identity, SAP credentials) still apply and those providers keep showing onboarding otherwise. Added a regression test: `AWS_REGION` alone is not a key and does not skip onboarding.

Good catch — fixed in 0093e45f1. You were right that this was not actually wired up: my first attempt only added `--no-mouse` to `createAuthCommand()`, which turns out to be test-only (`parseAuthCommandArgs`). The real `cline auth` path is the inline `authCmd` in `main.ts`, so the flag never reached `runInteractiveAuthTui`.

Now:
- `--no-mouse` is declared on the inline auth subcommand in `main.ts` and passed through to `runAuthCommand`.
- Resolution uses `getOptionValueSource("mouse") === "cli"` rather than the raw option value. Commander defaults a negatable `--no-mouse` to `true`, so reading `opts.mouse` directly would have silently clobbered the `CLINE_NO_MOUSE` / `CLINE_MOUSE` env fallback.
- Both flag positions work: `cline auth --no-mouse` and `cline --no-mouse auth` (auth flag wins, then root flag, then env).

Verified all five combinations resolve correctly, and added coverage in `auth.test.ts` for both the `--no-mouse` and absent cases.

This thread looks like a carry-over: the fix is present in `0093e45f1`, which is the commit this review ran against.

Tracing the full path end to end on that commit:

1. `main.ts` declares `--no-mouse` on the inline `authCmd` (the real runtime path), and resolves it with `getOptionValueSource("mouse") === "cli"` so Commander defaulting a negatable flag to `true` cannot clobber the env fallback. The auth flag wins, then the root flag:
```ts
const authMouse = (authCmd.getOptionValueSource("mouse") === "cli" ? authCmd.opts().mouse : undefined) ??
	(program.getOptionValueSource("mouse") === "cli" ? program.opts().mouse : undefined);
```
It is then passed as `mouse: authMouse` into `runAuthCommand({ ... })`.

2. `runAuthCommand(input)` forwards the same `input` object straight through to `runInteractiveAuthTui(input)` (no intermediate object is rebuilt, so `mouse` is not dropped).

3. `runInteractiveAuthTui` consumes it, preferring the flag and falling back to env only when the flag was not supplied:
```ts
const useMouse =
	input.mouse !== undefined
		? input.mouse
		: process.env.CLINE_NO_MOUSE !== "1" && process.env.CLINE_MOUSE !== "0";
```

Verified by simulating all five flag combinations against real Commander instances, all correct:

| invocation | resolved `mouse` |
|---|---|
| `auth` | `undefined` (env fallback) |
| `auth --no-mouse` | `false` |
| `--no-mouse auth` | `false` |
| `--no-mouse auth --no-mouse` | `false` |
| `auth -p anthropic` | `undefined` (env fallback) |

`cline auth --help` also lists `--no-mouse`, and `auth.test.ts` covers both the `--no-mouse` and absent cases.

The diff hunk this comment is anchored to predates the fix, which may be why the thread stayed open.
